## Root cause
The binding limit is the volume's provisioned throughput, not IOPS. vol-0123456789abcdef0 (gp3, 20 GiB, attached to i-1234567890abcdef0_5, a c6i.xlarge) is set to the gp3 baseline of 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s. The batch job started reading at about 18:05 UTC (no writes at all). From then on, read throughput has sat flat at 125.07 MiB/s in every 5-minute bucket, exactly the provisioned cap. The job only issues about 500 IOPS, about 17% of the 3,000 provisioned. Each read is 256 KiB (39,344,144,384 bytes ÷ 150,086 ops per 5 min), so 500 IOPS × 256 KiB = 125 MiB/s: the throughput cap is reached long before the IOPS cap. The instance is not the limit: its EBS byte and IO burst balances stayed at 99%. That is why IOPS looks normal. The alarm fired at 18:11:18 UTC on about 7.87 GB per minute (≈125 MiB/s, threshold 6 GB per minute). Fix: raise the volume's Throughput setting with an online ModifyVolume call, for example to 250–500 MiB/s, keeping IOPS at 3,000. The disk stays attached and the change needs no restart. A volume can only be modified about once every 6 hours, so pick the target once. The instance caps how far this helps. A c6i.xlarge has a baseline EBS bandwidth of about 156 MB/s (≈149 MiB/s) and bursts to about 1,250 MB/s for limited periods. If you need more than about 150 MiB/s for a long job, also move to a larger instance size (e.g. c6i.2xlarge or above) or plan for EBSByteBalance% to run down. Optionally raise the alarm threshold to match the new throughput.
## Evidence
- EC2 DescribeVolumes: vol-0123456789abcdef0 is gp3, 20 GiB, Iops=3000, Throughput=125 MiB/s, attached to i-1234567890abcdef0_5 (/dev/sdg).
- CloudWatch alarm example-b-gp3-read-bytes went to ALARM at 2026-11-23 18:11:18 UTC. Datapoints were about 7.869e9 bytes/60s (≈125 MiB/s) against a threshold of 6.0e9 (Sum, 60s period).
- AWS/EBS VolumeReadBytes (5-minute Sum) was 39,344,144,384–39,344,406,528 in every full bucket from 18:10 to 19:25 UTC, which is 125.07 MiB/s, pinned at the provisioned cap. The ramp-up starts in the 18:05 bucket.
- AWS/EBS VolumeReadOps is about 150,086 per 5 minutes (≈500 IOPS) and VolumeWriteOps is 0. That is about 17% of the 3,000 provisioned IOPS, so IOPS is not the limit.
- Each read averages 39,344,144,384 / 150,086 = 262,144 bytes (256 KiB). 500 IOPS × 256 KiB = 125 MiB/s, which is exactly the throughput ceiling.
- AWS/EBS VolumeQueueLength holds steady at about 1.5–2.0 throughout, consistent with requests waiting on a throughput-limited volume.
- AWS/EC2 EBSByteBalance% and EBSIOBalance% for i-1234567890abcdef0_5 stayed at a minimum of 99% from 18:00 to 19:30 UTC, so the instance's EBS bandwidth is not the limit.
## Affected resources
- vol-0123456789abcdef0
- i-1234567890abcdef0_5
- example-b-gp3-read-bytes
## Gaps
- VolumeThroughputExceededCheck and VolumeIOPSExceededCheck returned no datapoints, so the conclusion rests on throughput sitting exactly at the provisioned figure.
- No baseline from before 18:05 UTC exists (the workload started then), so "how fast the job used to run" cannot be measured from metrics.
- The c6i.xlarge EBS bandwidth figures (about 156 MB/s baseline, about 1,250 MB/s burst) are standard published specs and were not checked live. ", "signature": "", "type": "thinking"}, {"text": "Throughput is the binding dimension, not IOPS. The volume is stuck at exactly its provisioned 125 MiB/s while using only about 17% of its 3,000 IOPS. The fix is to raise the volume's Throughput setting, and if the job needs more than about 140 MiB/s for long, also move to a bigger instance.

**What the volume is doing**
- **Configuration:** vol-0123456789abcdef0 is gp3, 20 GiB, 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s, which are the gp3 defaults. It has never been modified, so no config change lowered it.
- **Throughput:** in every 5-minute window from 18:10 to 19:25 UTC it ran at 125.07 MiB/s, which is the cap. Almost all of it is reads.
- **IOPS:** about 500 per second against 3,000 provisioned.
- **Why IOPS looks normal:** each read is 256 KiB, and 500 × 256 KiB = 125 MiB/s. The throughput cap is hit long before the IOPS cap.
- **Queueing:** about 1.5 requests wait at a time and reads take about 3 ms. That fits a volume held back by throughput.
- **Alarm:** `example-b-gp3-read-bytes` went into ALARM at 18:11:18 UTC on about 7.87 GB per minute (≈125 MiB/s), against a 6 GB-per-minute threshold.
- **Timing:** the limit has applied since about 18:08 UTC, roughly 85 minutes ago, not just the last half hour. The job started when the instance was started at 18:05:10 UTC, so there is no earlier data to compare against.

**The instance is not the limit yet**
- **Current load:** the whole instance pushes about 133 MiB/s and 1,500 IOPS to EBS. A c6i.xlarge's baseline is 156.25 MB/s (≈149 MiB/s) and 6,000 IOPS.
- **Headroom:** its EBS burst balances (`EBSByteBalance%`, `EBSIOBalance%`) are at 99%, and AWS's checks for exceeding instance EBS throughput or IOPS read 0.
- **No per-volume confirmation:** AWS's "volume throughput exceeded" check returned no data for this volume. The conclusion rests on throughput sitting at exactly 125.07 MiB/s.

**What to change**
1. **Raise the volume's Throughput.** This is an online change with no detach or restart; leave IOPS at 3,000. gp3 allows up to 0.25 MiB/s per provisioned IOPS, so up to 750 MiB/s at 3,000 IOPS. You can only modify a volume about once every 6 hours, so pick the target once.
2. **Check whether the instance becomes the next limit.** Your other three volumes use about 8 MiB/s. That leaves this volume about 141 MiB/s sustained, which is only about 13% above today. Above that it runs on instance burst (up to 1,250 MB/s, for roughly 30 minutes a day).
   - For a long job, also resize the instance. A c6i.2xlarge has a 312.5 MB/s baseline and a c6i.4xlarge 625 MB/s. Resizing needs a stop/start.
   - Example pairings: about 250 MiB/s on a c6i.2xlarge, or 500 MiB/s or more on a c6i.4xlarge.
3. **Optionally move the alarm threshold** to match the new throughput.

{"id": "99e8a5fb460d44429c9712e88539b667", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "The background Task subagent assigned to task "propose-mitigation" successfully completed:

## Results
I've built and validated a mitigation plan, but haven't executed it. The main step raises the gp3 throughput on `vol-0123456789abcdef0` from 125 to 250 MiB/s while the volume stays attached, which should remove the cap holding the batch job back. It passed the safety check on the second attempt. The first attempt was rejected because it didn't save the current settings first or check the result after the change; both are now included.

What I checked just now:
- **Volume:** still gp3, 20 GiB, 3000 IOPS, 125 MiB/s, attached as `/dev/sdg` to `i-1234567890abcdef0_5`.
- **Instance:** still a running c6i.xlarge in us-east-1a.
- **Alarm:** still in ALARM. Its threshold is 6.0e9, and the last readings were about 7.87e9 bytes per minute, which works out to exactly the 125 MiB/s cap.

**Why 250 MiB/s:** the instance can sustain only about 141 MiB/s for this volume. Setting the volume above that means the volume is no longer the limit. The job can briefly reach 250 MiB/s using the instance's burst allowance. 250 is well within the 750 MiB/s that 3000 IOPS allows, so IOPS don't need to change. Expect about +$5 per month for the extra 125 MiB/s (roughly $0.04 per MiB/s-month above the free 125; check us-east-1 pricing).

The plan is for account 012345678901_1, region us-east-1.

## Execution plan

**1. Save the current settings (for rollback)**
```
aws ec2 describe-volumes --region us-east-1 --volume-ids vol-0123456789abcdef0 > vol-0123456789abcdef0.before.json
aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --region us-east-1 --alarm-names example-b-gp3-read-bytes > alarm.before.json
```
Confirm the volume shows `Iops=3000` and `Throughput=125`, and the alarm shows `Threshold=6.0e9`, Sum over 60 s, 3 of 3 datapoints.

**2. Check before changing**
```
aws ec2 describe-volumes-modifications --region us-east-1 --volume-ids vol-0123456789abcdef0
```
Go ahead only if this returns NotFound, or if the last modification is `completed` and more than 6 hours old. AWS allows one change to a volume about every 6 hours.

**3. Make the change**
- Raise the throughput. This happens while the volume stays attached, with no downtime:
  ```
  aws ec2 modify-volume --region us-east-1 --volume-id vol-0123456789abcdef0 --volume-type gp3 --iops 3000 --throughput 250
  ```
  - This starts the 6-hour lock, so no further change (including the rollback) is possible for about 6 hours.
- Optional: once the change reaches `optimizing` or `completed`, raise the alarm threshold to about 89% of the new throughput (250 MiB/s is about 1.573e10 bytes per minute):
  ```
  aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm --region us-east-1 --alarm-name example-b-gp3-read-bytes \
    --alarm-description "example test alarm, no actions" --namespace AWS/EBS --metric-name VolumeReadBytes \
    --dimensions Name=VolumeId,Value=vol-0123456789abcdef0 --statistic Sum --period 60 \
    --evaluation-periods 3 --datapoints-to-alarm 3 --threshold 14000000000 \
    --comparison-operator GreaterThanThreshold --treat-missing-data notBreaching
  ```

**4. Check the result**
- Watch the change until it reaches `optimizing` or `completed` with a target of 250 MiB/s:
  ```
  aws ec2 describe-volumes-modifications --region us-east-1 --volume-ids vol-0123456789abcdef0
  ```
  The new throughput applies once it reaches `optimizing`.
- Confirm the volume shows `Throughput=250`, `Iops=3000`, `State=in-use`:
  ```
  aws ec2 describe-volumes --region us-east-1 --volume-ids vol-0123456789abcdef0
  ```
- Confirm the alarm shows the new threshold (if you changed it) and returns to OK:
  ```
  aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --region us-east-1 --alarm-names example-b-gp3-read-bytes
  ```
- Watch the job's read rate and the instance's burst balance for 30–60 minutes. `VolumeReadBytes` per minute should rise above about 7.87e9, which means the job is reading faster than 125 MiB/s:
  ```
  aws cloudwatch get-metric-data --region us-east-1 --start-time <now-1h> --end-time <now> --metric-data-queries \
  '[{"Id":"r","MetricStat":{"Metric":{"Namespace":"AWS/EBS","MetricName":"VolumeReadBytes","Dimensions":[{"Name":"VolumeId","Value":"vol-0123456789abcdef0"}]},"Period":60,"Stat":"Sum"}},
    {"Id":"b","MetricStat":{"Metric":{"Namespace":"AWS/EC2","MetricName":"EBSByteBalance%","Dimensions":[{"Name":"InstanceId","Value":"i-1234567890abcdef0_5"}]},"Period":300,"Stat":"Minimum"}}]'
  ```
  If `EBSByteBalance%` falls toward 0, the instance becomes the limit at about 141 MiB/s for this volume. See the follow-up below.

**5. Undo if needed**
- Set the throughput back to 125 MiB/s. This only works after the 6-hour lock ends, and it also happens without downtime:
  ```
  aws ec2 modify-volume --region us-east-1 --volume-id vol-0123456789abcdef0 --volume-type gp3 --iops 3000 --throughput 125
  ```
- If you changed the alarm, run the same `put-metric-alarm` command as in step 3 with `--threshold 6000000000`.

## If the job needs more than about 141 MiB/s sustained
This step needs downtime, so I left it out of the validated plan. Do it as a planned maintenance step after the job pauses.
1. Stop the job, then stop the instance and wait:
   ```
   aws ec2 stop-instances --region us-east-1 --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0_5
   aws ec2 wait instance-stopped --region us-east-1 --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0_5
   ```
2. Change the instance type:
   ```
   aws ec2 modify-instance-attribute --region us-east-1 --instance-id i-1234567890abcdef0_5 --instance-type "{\"Value\":\"c6i.2xlarge\"}"
   ```
   - c6i.2xlarge sustains 312.5 MB/s; use c6i.4xlarge (625 MB/s) if you need more.
3. Start it again, then check that all four volumes are still attached at the same device names:
   ```
   aws ec2 start-instances --region us-east-1 --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0_5
   ```
- To undo, stop the instance, set it back to `c6i.xlarge`, and start it.
- Risks: the job is interrupted, the instance costs about twice as much, and its public IP changes if it has no Elastic IP.

## Durable prevention
The volume was created with the gp3 defaults (3000 IOPS / 125 MiB/s), which this read-heavy job can fill.
- **What to change:** wherever this volume is defined (Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK or a launch template), set `Throughput` to the value you end up using, 250 or more. Make sure the instance type's sustained EBS throughput covers the job plus about 8 MiB/s for the other volumes. Set the alarm threshold relative to the provisioned throughput, at about 85–90% of the cap.
- **Done when:** a fresh deployment comes up with the new throughput and alarm threshold. Also, re-applying the configuration must not undo the manual change.

Things I couldn't cover:
- I don't know how much throughput the job actually needs. Before today's start at 18:05 there is no earlier data to compare against, and it ran at the cap the whole time.
- AWS reports `EbsOptimized=false` for this instance. c6i instances are normally EBS-optimized anyway, and the instance limits in the findings already assume that, but it's worth a quick check.
- No pipeline or code change caused this, so there is nothing to roll back.

# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### VolumeReadBytes alarm in ALARM on vol-0123456789abcdef0
**Description:** Alarm example-b-gp3-read-bytes changed to ALARM at 2026-11-23 18:11:18 UTC. The last 3 one-minute datapoints were about 7.87e9 bytes each (Sum), against a threshold of 6e9. Alarm ARN: [redacted ARN].
**Time:** 2026-11-23T18:08:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: Read workload is saturating gp3 provisioned throughput (125 MiB/s)
**Description:** Since the instance started at 18:05 UTC, the batch job's 256 KiB sequential reads have driven vol-0123456789abcdef0 to exactly its provisioned 125 MiB/s, the gp3 default. The volume uses only about 500 of its 3,000 IOPS (500 × 256 KiB = 125 MiB/s). The volume has never been modified, so it was always provisioned at the default. The instance is not the limit: it drives about 133 MiB/s against a 156.25 MB/s baseline, with burst balances at 99%.
**Cascades to:** symptom-gp3-read-bytes-alarm

#### Supporting Observations
- **gp3 volume provisioned at baseline 3000 IOPS / 125 MiB/s:** vol-0123456789abcdef0 is a 20 GiB gp3 volume (unencrypted, us-east-1a), attached as /dev/sdg to i-1234567890abcdef0_5 (c6i.xlarge, example-perf, launched 2026-11-23 18:05 UTC). The instance also has vol-1234567890abcdef0_20, vol-1234567890abcdef0_4 and vol-1234567890abcdef0_16 attached. Reads of about 7.87e9 bytes/min work out to roughly 131 MB/s, or about 125 MiB/s, which is the volume's provisioned throughput.

#### Gaps
- **No data from VolumeThroughputExceededCheck:** The per-volume VolumeThroughputExceededCheck and VolumeIOPSExceededCheck metrics returned no datapoints for vol-0123456789abcdef0. The saturation conclusion rests on throughput sitting at exactly the 125.07 MiB/s cap, not on a direct exceeded-check signal.

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Raise gp3 throughput on vol-0123456789abcdef0 from 125 to 250 MiB/s online (IOPS stay at 3000)

## Reasoning
Throughput, not IOPS, is the binding limit. The instance sustains only ~141 MiB/s for this volume, so 250 MiB/s takes the volume out of the bottleneck and lets the job use instance burst. 250 is well under the 750 MiB/s that 3000 IOPS allows. Cost is about +$5/month. Validated, not executed; account 012345678901_1, us-east-1.

## Execution Plan

### Step 1: Prepare

#### 1.1 Capture volume and alarm config
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 describe-volumes --region us-east-1 --volume-ids vol-0123456789abcdef0 > vol-0123456789abcdef0.before.json
aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --region us-east-1 --alarm-names example-b-gp3-read-bytes > alarm.before.json
```
**Purpose:** Capture volume and alarm config. Confirm Iops=3000, Throughput=125, Threshold=6.0e9 (Sum/60s, 3 of 3).

### Step 2: Pre Validate

#### 2.1 Proceed only if NotFound or last modification is completed and older…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 describe-volumes-modifications --region us-east-1 --volume-ids vol-0123456789abcdef0
```
**Purpose:** Proceed only if NotFound or last modification is completed and older than 6 hours.

### Step 3: Apply

#### 3.1 Lift the 125 MiB/s cap with no detach or downtime
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 modify-volume --region us-east-1 --volume-id vol-0123456789abcdef0 --volume-type gp3 --iops 3000 --throughput 250
```
**Purpose:** Lift the 125 MiB/s cap with no detach or downtime.
**Risks:** Starts a ~6-hour modification lock; no further change, including rollback, for ~6 hours, About +$5/month for the extra 125 MiB/s

#### 3.2 Optional: move the alarm threshold to ~89% of the new cap once the…
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm --region us-east-1 --alarm-name example-b-gp3-read-bytes \
  --alarm-description "example test alarm, no actions" --namespace AWS/EBS --metric-name VolumeReadBytes \
  --dimensions Name=VolumeId,Value=vol-0123456789abcdef0 --statistic Sum --period 60 \
  --evaluation-periods 3 --datapoints-to-alarm 3 --threshold 14000000000 \
  --comparison-operator GreaterThanThreshold --treat-missing-data notBreaching
```
**Purpose:** Optional: move the alarm threshold to ~89% of the new cap once the change reaches optimizing.

### Step 4: Post Validate

#### 4.1 Confirm state optimizing/completed and Throughput=250, Iops=3000…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 describe-volumes-modifications --region us-east-1 --volume-ids vol-0123456789abcdef0
aws ec2 describe-volumes --region us-east-1 --volume-ids vol-0123456789abcdef0
```
**Purpose:** Confirm state optimizing/completed and Throughput=250, Iops=3000, State=in-use.

#### 4.2 Confirm the new threshold (if changed) and that the alarm returns to OK
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --region us-east-1 --alarm-names example-b-gp3-read-bytes
```
**Purpose:** Confirm the new threshold (if changed) and that the alarm returns to OK.

#### 4.3 Watch 30–60 min: reads should exceed ~7.87e9 bytes/min
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-data --region us-east-1 --start-time <now-1h> --end-time <now> --metric-data-queries \
'[{"Id":"r","MetricStat":{"Metric":{"Namespace":"AWS/EBS","MetricName":"VolumeReadBytes","Dimensions":[{"Name":"VolumeId","Value":"vol-0123456789abcdef0"}]},"Period":60,"Stat":"Sum"}},
  {"Id":"b","MetricStat":{"Metric":{"Namespace":"AWS/EC2","MetricName":"EBSByteBalance%","Dimensions":[{"Name":"InstanceId","Value":"i-1234567890abcdef0_5"}]},"Period":300,"Stat":"Minimum"}}]'
```
**Purpose:** Watch 30–60 min: reads should exceed ~7.87e9 bytes/min.
**Advisory:** If EBSByteBalance% falls toward 0, the instance becomes the limit at ~141 MiB/s; plan a resize to c6i.2xlarge (312.5 MB/s) or c6i.4xlarge (625 MB/s), which needs a stop/start.

### Step 5: Rollback

#### 5.1 Restore 125 MiB/s online, after the 6-hour lock ends
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 modify-volume --region us-east-1 --volume-id vol-0123456789abcdef0 --volume-type gp3 --iops 3000 --throughput 125
```
**Purpose:** Restore 125 MiB/s online, after the 6-hour lock ends.

#### 5.2 Restore the original alarm threshold
**Type:** text
If the alarm was changed, re-run the step 3 put-metric-alarm command with --threshold 6000000000.
**Purpose:** Restore the original alarm threshold.

## Code Change Specification

### Requirements

#### 1. Codify the throughput and alarm settings
**Description:** Wherever this volume is defined (Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK or launch template), set Throughput to the value in use (250+). Make sure the instance's sustained EBS throughput covers the job plus ~8 MiB/s for the other volumes, and set the alarm threshold to ~85–90% of provisioned throughput.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- A fresh deployment comes up with the new throughput and alarm threshold
- Re-applying the configuration does not undo the manual change

Other attached volumes (vol-1234567890abcdef0_20 gp3 root, vol-1234567890abcdef0_4 io2, vol-1234567890abcdef0_16 gp3) use about 8 MiB/s combined.
- Implication: if only the gp3 throughput is raised, sustained gains are capped near about 141 MiB/s for this volume (the instance baseline of about 149 MiB/s minus about 8 MiB/s used by the other volumes) once the instance's EBS burst balance is gone. Volumes can be modified only about once every 6 hours. (2) If the job needs more than about 141 MiB/s sustained, resize the instance (for example to c6i.2xlarge or larger; this needs a stop/start) to lift the instance EBS baseline. (3) Optionally retune the alarm threshold to the new throughput.", "type": "text"}], "user_reference": null}
